title: A polygon node fills a shape given by its points
body:
acre draws rectangles, ellipses, and straight or routed lines. It has no node for a shape given by its points.

The cloud-search figure draws three regions of a 260 by 362 DP matrix. They are the forward cloud, the backward cloud, and the row bounds made from the two. Each region's edge is a staircase of a few hundred points. With no shape node, `gen_cloud.py` drew the forward cloud as 517 `line` nodes, one per anti-diagonal, wide enough to touch their neighbours. It drew the row bounds as 278 one-row `box` nodes. The alignment path through the matrix took 327 more `line` nodes, one per step.

## Proposal

- `polygon { points X Y X Y ...; }` fills and strokes a closed shape, with the usual `fill`, `stroke`, `stroke-width` and `dash`.
- `polyline { points X Y X Y ...; }` strokes an open path, and takes `head` and `tail` like `line`.

Each region above becomes one node. A list of several hundred points still comes from a program, so this pairs with the issue on reading numbers from a data file.

## Open

- Whether `points` takes cell coordinates and a scale, so a staircase in matrix cells can be written without multiplying each value by the cell size.
close_reason: Landed on dev in 023610e. `polygon` and `polyline` nodes (`Polygon` and `Polyline` in `scene/diagram.rs`), attachable by name and changed by a timeline like other shapes. Cell coordinates for `points` stay with acre-4d72e1.
